 | Aircraft | 8.675 ± 0.874 | 01:59 |

+\*Not from the draft: measured on 547 cases with the finest and solid cells excluded (92,837 nodes), three seeds, sample standard deviation, on a single NVIDIA H100, so its training time is not directly comparable with the rows above. On this case NUNO (6.805 ± 0.087) and L-SplineFNO on a denser latent grid (6.651 ± 0.168) have lower mean error.
 
 The comparison includes Transolver, UPT, MSPT, GNOT, NUNO, GINO, and analytic SplineFNO at approximately matched parameter counts. L-SplineFNO has the lowest mean relative error on heat sink, heated duct, and HIVE, and improves on analytic SplineFNO on all five cases. Attention models achieve lower errors on bracket and aircraft. L-SplineFNO trains faster than MSPT and GNOT on all five cases, while Transolver and UPT are faster on some cases. These results support a competitive accuracy–cost trade-off, with performance depending on the benchmark.

+def thin_nodes_for_plot(config, node_coords, *tensors, default_cap=60000):
+    """Cap the node count a scatter plot renders, returning thinned copies.
+
+    Plotly writes every point into the HTML, so a full-mesh cloud produces a
+    file no browser can open: MAST-U at 29,183,754 nodes wrote 2.7 GB per
+    variable, six files and 16.6 GB for one run, and filled a 50 GB $HOME.
+    Nothing is learned from those points either -- a scatter of 29M spheres is
+    the silhouette of the machine at any zoom.
+
+    The draw is a fixed-seed uniform subsample, sorted, so the same nodes are
+    shown by every panel of a run and by every run on a shared mesh. It is NOT
+    volume-weighted: this is a picture, and the reported metrics are computed
+    on the full field upstream of here.
+
+    ``Viz.max_plot_nodes`` overrides the cap; 0 or null disables thinning and
+    restores the previous behaviour exactly. Clouds at or below the cap are
+    passed through untouched, which is every other benchmark in the tree (FDS
+    116,928 is the largest, and it thins by less than 2x).
+
+    The node axis is dim 2 of ``[BS, vars, N_nodes(, Nt)]``; anything with
+    fewer than three dimensions, and None, is returned as it came.
+    """
+    cap = (config or {}).get('Viz', {}).get('max_plot_nodes', default_cap)
+    n_nodes = node_coords.shape[0]
+    if not cap or n_nodes <= int(cap):
+        return (node_coords,) + tensors
+    cap = int(cap)
+    sub = np.sort(np.random.default_rng(0).choice(n_nodes, cap, replace=False))
+    print(f"  Plot thinned to {cap:,} of {n_nodes:,} nodes "
+          f"(Viz.max_plot_nodes); metrics are on the full field.")
+    out = [node_coords[sub]]
+    for tensor in tensors:
+        if tensor is None or getattr(tensor, 'ndim', 0) < 3:
+            out.append(tensor)
+        else:
+            out.append(tensor[:, :, sub])
+    return tuple(out)
+
+
